messages:
lee-kotlin: FYI found a weird hang when using our suspend-based Retrofit calls + Authenticator that does a blocking token refresh. only reproducible on API 30 emulator.

lee-kotlin: flow: suspend call -> okhttp dispatch executes -> Authenticator.detects 401 -> runBlocking refresh inside authenticate() -> subsequent retries never finish (client stuck waiting).

nina-qa: can you paste the snippet? curious whether it's an Authenticator vs Interceptor difference.

lee-kotlin: sure, simplified: 
``` 
class TokenAuthenticator : Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    // blocks waiting for coroutine refresh
    runBlocking { TokenService.refresh() }
    return response.request.newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${TokenService.token}")
      .build()
  }
}
```

lee-kotlin: Retrofit call is declared as suspend fun generate(...): CompletionResult. Using okhttp 4.x.

brad-platform: 2 quick notes: (1) Authenticator callbacks run on OkHttp's internal threads and runBlocking will block them, potentially preventing connection cleanup; (2) Interceptor vs Authenticator semantics differ when it comes to retrying on auth failures and with multiplexed HTTP/2 streams this can starve the queue.

nina-qa: repro steps? want to add to flaky-emulator suite.

lee-kotlin: steps: (1) emulator API 30, (2) run app that calls suspend generate in quick succession (~10 concurrent), (3) have TokenService simulate slow network refresh (~800ms) and occasionally throw to force multiple retries. After ~20s, new requests hang in our app.

brad-platform: suggestion: avoid runBlocking in Authenticator; use an async refresh that writes token to persistent storage and let subsequent requests pick it up, or preemptively refresh tokens before making calls. Also add a small safety timeout in authenticate() to bail if refresh takes >1s and return null so OkHttp fails fast.

lee-kotlin: implemented a patch that moves refresh to a synchronized non-blocking path: we use a singleflight-like mutex + coroutineScope.runBlocking with very short timeout and a fallback error. smells gross but removes the hang in emulator.

nina-qa: I'll add a matrix job to the flaky-emulator pipeline to exercise suspend-call + token refresh races across API 28-31 and check that no request remains in RUNNING state longer than 5s.

sam-ci-bot: queued flaky test job: emulator-matrix-token-race (job id 7982).

brad-platform: also please add a note in SDK docs: "Do not use runBlocking in OkHttp Authenticator / Interceptor callbacks; use non-blocking refresh and cap retries". We should have parity across Java and Kotlin SDKs: Java SDK currently uses synchronous refresh on executor threads which worked because we use a dedicated executor; Kotlin SDK was relying on coroutine threads and accidentally used OkHttp threads.

lee-kotlin: filing issue and PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-kotlin/issues/911 (PR incoming) with test harness and docs change.

nina-qa: will validate PR on emulator farm once CI runs.

lee-kotlin: thanks all, will follow up if flaky job still shows occurrences. :raised_hands:
